Their products with background $\theta$ may be signed before multiplication by the cutoff, but their local expansions in bounded plurisubharmonic Hessians and fixed smooth forms are continuous under capacity convergence. edits.old: The Fredholm argument in the proof of \cref{thm:gauduchon} applies also in the presence of first-order terms. For clarity, deform the elliptic operator to a Laplacian to see that its index is zero. Its adjoint for $\eta_u^n$ has a one-dimensional real smooth kernel. A generator has nonzero integral, since otherwise the Fredholm alternative would solve $\mathcal L_uv=1$. Normalize that integral to one. If the generator were negative somewhere, a nonnegative test function supported there, minus its negative weighted integral, would again give a strictly positive right side in the range of $\mathcal L_u$, contradicting the maximum principle. Thus the generator is nonnegative. Applying the strong minimum principle to its adjoint equation after subtracting the positive part of the zeroth-order coefficient makes it strictly positive. This is exactly the positivity argument of \cref{thm:gauduchon}, and gives the asserted $\rho_u$ and uniqueness.
edits.new: The Fredholm and positivity arguments in the proof of \cref{thm:gauduchon} apply to this real elliptic operator with first-order terms and no zeroth-order term. Its index is zero by deformation to a Laplacian, so the adjoint for $\eta_u^n$ has a one-dimensional smooth kernel with a strictly positive generator. Normalizing its integral to one gives $\rho_u$ and uniqueness.

edits.old:
The index is zero: the principal elliptic coefficients can be joined through positive coefficients to a fixed scalar Laplacian, whose index is zero, while the lower-order terms can be continuously removed. Its cokernel is therefore one-dimensional. For the logarithmic determinant equation the full derivative in $(u,b)$ is
\[
 (w,c)\longmapsto Lw-(n-1)c.
\]
Given any H\"older function $f$, take $c=-(n-1)^{-1}\int_Xf\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ and solve $Lw=f+(n-1)c$ with zero $\gamma^n$ mean. This gives a bounded inverse on the corresponding H\"older spaces. Positivity of $\Gamma_u$ is an open condition, so the implicit function theorem proves openness of the solution parameters.
edits.new: For a prescribed right side $f$, its adjoint probability determines $c=-\int_Xf\,\mathrm{d}\mu_u^\gamma$; the Fredholm alternative then gives a unique mean-zero $w$, with a bounded inverse by Schauder estimates. Since positivity of $\Gamma_u$ is open, the implicit function theorem proves openness of the solution parameters.
